title: Modified resins and their uses
abstract: Modified thermoplastic hydrocarbon thermoplastic resins are provided, as well as methods for their manufacture and uses thereof in rubber compositions. Modified thermoplastic resins are modified by decreasing the relative amount of dimer, trimer, tetramer, and pentamer oligomers compared to the corresponding unmodified thermoplastic resin polymers, resulting in a product that exhibits a greater change in the glass transition temperature of the elastomer(s) used in tire formulations. This results in better viscoelastic predictors of tire tread performance such as wet grip and rolling resistance. Modified thermoplastic resins impart remarkable properties to various rubber compositions, such as tires, belts, hoses, brakes and the like. Automotive tires incorporating modified thermoplastic resins have been shown to have excellent results in balancing the properties of rolling resistance, tire wear, snow performance and wet braking performance.
